name: Woodward, Inc.
moat_justification: Certified, specified-in content on long-lived commercial and defense platforms with a services/aftermarket annuity and demonstrated pricing power (~8% in FY26); held back from 8+ by customer concentration (top 5 ~36% of revenue), dependence on Boeing/Airbus build rates, and a front-loaded capacity-capex phase whose returns start late CY28.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 13 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.7% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 6.9x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) aero/industrial controls franchise executing well, but at $333.27 the TTM OE yield is 1.7% and even the super-bull IRR is 10.6% — weighted IRR 6.4%, IV@15% $88.26; clears 15% only below ~$88.
moat_for: Sole-source / specified-in positions on major platforms — certification lock-in for the platform's life
Decades-long platform lives plus high-margin aftermarket/services annuity (Q3 FY26 commercial services +24%, defense services +20%)
Deep fuel-system and actuation know-how, extended into electrification via the Safran electromechanical actuation acquisition
Demonstrated pricing power — ~8% companywide pricing in FY26
moat_against: Customer concentration — top 5 customers ~36% of revenue
Hostage to Boeing/Airbus production schedules and program health
Pricing guided to normalize from ~8% to 3-5%; OEM pricing pressure at concentrated customers
Heavy front-loaded capex phase (A350 spoiler-actuator facility, deliveries from late CY28) depresses near-term OE
Cyclical aero/industrial end-markets; China on-highway exit drag
